Fair enough :) I'm curious what metrics you are referring to though.

Oh sorry! Its our Net Expected Points (NEP) metric.

So we have historical data that tells us over the past 15 years, how many points a team can expect to score in a given down and distance situation. This then allows us to judge the contributions or detractions of any given play to a team's chances of scoring. A play that improves a team's chances of scoring gets a positive score and vice-versa for a negative play. This way we can quantify the actual contributions of a player rather than their raw numbers, so a 5 yard run on 3rd and 4 (which results in a first down and keeps the chains moving) would be worth far more than a 5 yard run on 3rd and 20 (which results in a punt and was probably done against a team pulling back its coverage).

In regards to Charles Sims, I believe he had one of the worst NEP per touch (something around -0.24 per carry, meaning every time he ran the ball he was costing his team a quarter of a point, in terms of historical projections that is) whereas Doug Martin was actually fairly average. I wrote about it pretty in depth over here too if interested: https://www.numberfire.com/nfl/news/5576/what-is-doug-martin-s-fantasy-football-value-in-2015
